data.name: Fathan
data.long_meaning: The name Fathan is derived from the Arabic root 'fatha' which means 'to open'. In Islamic context, it is mentioned in the Hadith that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) used this name for his horse. The name is also said to symbolize the spiritual opening of one's eyes to the truth and guidance of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tabari, The History of al-Tabari, Vol. II, p. 683 The name Fathan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the Battle of Siffin, the forces of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan clashed. Both leaders rode white horses, Ali on his horse named Murad, and Muawiya on his horse named Fathan. The battle ended in a stalemate, and eventually, the matter was resolved through arbitration, not through military victory.
